newsitem.title: USA: Colorado ACLU sues state over green card.
newsitem.headline: Colorado ACLU sues state over green card.

text.p: The American Civil Liberties Union of Colorado Wednesday sued a state agency for confiscating a green card from a legal permanent resident from El Salvador because a state employee believed it was invalid.

The employee confiscated the card when Maria Juventina Flores applied for a Colorado state identification card at the Division of Motor Vehicles. The DMV then lost the green card, forcing Flores to cancel a trip home to see her ailing mother.

The card was valid but she was afraid she would not be able to return to the United States if she did not have the document, ACLU legal director Mark Silverstein said. "There is no state or federal law that authorises Colorado employees to confiscate immigration documents that are issued by the federal government," he said.

The ACLU filed its lawsuit in state court, alleging the state's action was in violation of the Fourth Amendment, which prohibits unreasonable search and seizure. It is seeking unspecified damages from the state and a declaration that the confiscation policy is unconstitutional.
